job.title: Geochemist
job.description:
Geochemists - Graduate through to Senior
 
My client is a well-established, specialist Geochemistry focused consultancy servicing the mining and resources sector in Australia and internationally.
 
They are not a big multidisciplinary firm where geochemistry is a side offering. It is what they do, and they are recognised globally for it and have longstanding relationships and repeat business with a range of clients due to quality work and reputation. They have been around for decades and developed a number of the test methods now used across the industry.
 
Due to their strong forward pipeline of contracted work, they are expanding and are currently recruiting several geochemists at various levels from Graduate to Senior.
 
What you would be doing
 
  • Geochemical assessments of mine and infrastructure projects, from compiling geological and assay data through to interpreting what it means for materials management and closure
  • Designing sampling programmes, then preparing and managing the laboratory test programmes that follow
  • Assessing ARD and NMD potential and building the management plans around it
  • Contributing to project approvals, PRCP submissions and closure plans
  • Working across the full project life, from exploration and feasibility through operations to closure, rather than being stuck at one stage
  • Site visits and field sampling
  • Supporting the water services team on hydrology and hydrogeology work
  • Writing the technical reports that go to clients and regulators
 
What you will need
 
  • A degree in geology, chemistry, environmental geochemistry or similar
  • Experience in environmental consulting or with a mining company
  • An understanding of material characterisation, including static and kinetic leachate data
  • Good technical writing
  • Experience in software such as PHREEQC or similar, and GIS, are useful but not essential
 
My client is flexible on background and whilst Geology or chemistry is the usual route, they have people who came in from other backgrounds - time on a mine site, and understanding how a site actually runs, is highly regarded.
 
You also do not need to have been a consultant - if you are doing this work inside a mining company and fancy the move, they are interested in chatting.
 
What's on offer
 
  • Good salary, negotiable depending on your experience (call for a confidential chat)
  • An annual bonus on top of base salary, at every level
  • Perth or Brisbane ideally (other locations also considered)
  • Real international work. They operate in more than 30 countries and are not constrained by geography, so a Perth-based geochemist might spend time on projects in Asia or Africa
  • Multi-commodity work with clients ranging from juniors to the majors, so you are not tied to one commodity or one account
  • They are expanding, including a new arm overseas, so there is room to move up rather than wait for someone to retire
  • A clear graded structure, so you know what the next step up looks like and what it takes to get there
  • Their service lines are shaped by the people they hire. If you are strong in something and there is a business case, they will back you to build it
  • Specialists around you, including several PhD-level people, and an in-house ARD laboratory
  • Genuine technical mentoring from people who have spent their whole careers in this niche
  • Small enough that you are not a number. Direct access to the principals and a real say in how the work gets done
  • Plenty of the work is advice, interpretation and building management plans with clients, not just sitting behind a bench
  • City based, not FIFO or residential. Site travel comes up a few times a year, in blocks of a week or two
  • Hybrid working with set office days, and support for conferences, professional development and training
  • A friendly, relaxed environment and a genuinely good team culture
  • A well-established, stable and growing company with an exciting pipeline of work ahead

job.title: Environmental Project Manager
job.description:
Gather Recruitment specialise in connecting great people with leading organisations in the environmental sector. We're currently partnering with a leading West Australian company who are experts in carbon offset and revegetation.
 
They help organisations deliver on their environmental commitments through revegetation and reforestation projects that generate Australian Carbon Credit Units and create long-term, biodiverse landscapes that benefit WA's ecology and communities for generations to come.
 
The role

The business is growing and due to internal promotion, there's now an opening for an experienced Project Manager to come in and run project delivery for both existing and new work.
 
It's a diverse, hands-on role with real variety and the chance to do something genuinely meaningful. You'll be involved across the full spectrum - site selection and preparation, plant selection and supply, planting and implementation, monitoring and maintenance - working alongside a small, capable team of project managers.
 
This is a 12-month contract initially, but with a strong pipeline of work already secured well into 2027, there's a very good chance it will roll on well beyond that.
 
The responsibilities
 
  • Project planning - develop and deliver revegetation projects from site selection through to completion
  • Stakeholder engagement - build positive relationships with landowners, clients and the wider team
  • Site management - site assessments, land prep, planting and ongoing maintenance
  • Team and subcontractors - manage a small delivery team and a crew of subcontractors on the ground
  • Budgeting - control project budgets, allocate resources and coordinate procurement
  • Monitoring and reporting - track performance and prepare project reports (templates provided, nothing academic)
 
The experience

You might come from carbon offset, revegetation, forestry, construction, water or agricultural work, or you may be a botanist, ecologist or environmental scientist with solid project management under your belt. Either way, to do well here you'll ideally have:
 
  • Previous experience in a field-based role and the desire and ability to work in the field
  • Project Management experience
  • Subcontractor management experience
  • Good organisation, budgeting and planning skills
  • Independent and self-motivated, and happy to adapt 
  • Good communication skills and the ability to fit into a small, friendly team
  • Ideally some technical environmental knowledge or qualificaitons such as BSc in an environmental subject (preferred, but not essential) - conservation or botany knowledge is a real plus
 
The journey

A big part of what makes this role special is the time you'll spend out in the field on country. You'll work in some genuinely beautiful parts of regional WA and watch projects come to life, from bare paddock to thriving native landscape. Not many jobs offer that.
 
During the winter planting season (roughly May to August) this is where it all happens, so you'll spend stretches drive-in drive-out Monday to Friday and home at weekends. You'll stay in comfortable accommodation with all expenses covered, and bank Time in Lieu that you take as a proper break once the season winds down. Outside of the planting season it's much lighter, just a handful of days a month.
 
It's hands-on, it's rewarding, and the field team is a good one. It's not a desk job though, so you'll need to genuinely enjoy getting out there.
 
The benefits
 
  • Good salary, negotiable depending on your experience (call for a confidential chat)
  • Company vehicle for work use and travel to and from work
  • Time in Lieu accrued for field time over 38 hours, usually taken as a block after the season or over the holidays
  • Laptop, and a work phone or phone allowance
  • Some working from home flexibility outside the planting season
  • A friendly, relaxed environment and a genuinely good team culture
  • A well-established, stable and growing company with an exciting pipeline of work ahead
 
This is a great opportunity to join a supportive company that values its people, has big plans for the future, and is committed to restoring Western Australia's unique landscapes and protecting biodiversity.
